summary.headline: Asarfi Hospital FY26 consolidated revenue rose 42% to INR173.5 crore and PAT 58% to INR16.7 crore; Q4 revenue INR45.2 crore (+29%).
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 42% YoY to INR173.5 crore with EBITDA of INR35.3 crore (20% margin) and PAT of INR16.7 crore (10% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR45.2 crore (+29% YoY), EBITDA INR7.7 crore (17% margin) and PAT INR3.9 crore (+9% YoY). Cancer hospital occupancy improved to 42% but Q4 patient volumes dipped due to Jharkhand government scheme approval delays. Management reiterated a Vision 2028 target of 500+ beds, INR400 crore revenue and 23-25% EBITDA margin, and guided FY27 revenue of INR260 crore and at least 22% EBITDA margin; several timelines (bone marrow transplant, acquisition, merger) have slipped.

segments.name: Super specialty hospital (285 beds)
segments.commentary: ARPOB improved to INR23,000; total surgeries up 26% YoY to over 6,300 procedures. Cardiac beds raised from 25 to 45; Philips Azurion cath lab operational from March 2026. Cardiology, General Medicine and Neurosurgery are top contributors; Orthopedic among fastest growing in Q4.

segments.name: Cancer hospital (65 beds)
segments.commentary: Occupancy rose to 42% in FY26; revenue INR33 crore vs INR20 crore in FY25. Ayushman Bharat contributes about 15% of cancer revenue; cancer contributes 10-12% of group revenue. Q4 patient numbers fell on Jharkhand scheme approval delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR260 crore, including organic growth and an acquisition (management described the mix as organic and inorganic); management said it is 'confident' but gave no quarterly split.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of at least 22%; Vision 2028 targets 23-25% EBITDA margin, INR400 crore revenue and 500+ beds.
FY27 PAT margin target of 13-15%, supported by case-mix changes and cost management.
Cancer hospital to expand from 65 to 150 beds within about two years at INR2-3 crore capex, funded from internal accruals; management also reiterated 1,000 beds before FY30.
Bone marrow transplant unit delayed pending Jharkhand organ transplant policy approval; management expects it in about 4-5 months, with little revenue in FY27 and meaningful contribution in FY28.
Management plans to migrate to the main board of exchanges and expects eligibility after July 2026.
capex_capacity: Cancer hospital bed expansion from 65 to 150 beds: INR2-3 crore capex, funded through internal accruals as existing OT and ICU are in place.
Healthcare Management Research Institute (under construction): capex of about INR8-10 crore expected in the coming year.
Total current-year capex stated as less than INR15 crore, per the analyst's INR10-12 crore estimate plus INR2-3 crore for capacity unlocking.
Cash on hand INR8-10 crore; management said no debt is planned currently, but debt may be considered for major capex.
demand_pricing: Cardiac capacity expanded by about 20 beds in Q4 FY26; patient flow rising after outreach to 10 neighbouring districts.
Management says there is no comparable cancer hospital in the region and only Jharkhand has under 500 operational oncology beds; Asarfi is one of three dedicated cancer hospitals in the state.
Ayushman Bharat and government schemes carry low package rates; management prefers schemes with better rates.
Receivable ageing is around six to seven months; management said debtor realisation improved from the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Ayushman Bharat scheme impact and share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ayushman Bharat operates only at the cancer hospital, contributing about 15% of cancer revenue; the company prioritises schemes with better package rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bone marrow transplant facility not yet live despite the FY26 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharkhand lacks a settled organ transplant policy, so approval is delayed; doctors are hired and only permission is pending, with about 4-5 months expected and minimal FY27 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the promoter's proposed hospital merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Delayed because heirs of two or three deceased shareholders have not inherited their shares; management expects completion in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cancer patient numbers fall in Q4, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: A new Jharkhand government scheme and approval-system changes caused administrative delays; management says approvals are now normal and does not expect impact this year.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 22%, against 20% achieved in FY26; the long-term target is 23-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR260 crore FY27 revenue guidance achievable and does it include acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident; guidance is a mix of organic growth from the super specialty and cancer hospitals and inorganic growth from an acquisition that management said is nearly settled, pending technical issues.

risks_watch: Receivables and working capital: ageing of six to seven months and reimbursement delays from government schemes.
Execution risk on the INR260 crore FY27 revenue and 400 crore Vision 2028 targets, with Q4 revenue of INR45.2 crore annualising well below FY27 guidance.
Regulatory and policy dependence: Jharkhand scheme approvals, organ transplant policy and political uncertainty affecting government payments.
Delayed bone marrow transplant unit, acquisition and merger, all of which have slipped past earlier timelines.
Management did not provide the cancer hospital margin or utilisation outlook on the call; the answer was deferred to email. Other income of INR3.66 crore in March 2025 also awaits a breakdown.
Possible debt funding if large capex opportunities arise, given ROE below growth rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on growth targets, especially cancer hospital and acquisitions, but cautious on government processes. Management was evasive on specifics such as cancer margins, utilisation, other income and the merger, deferring them to email.
key_quotes: So, now it is time to be aggressive.
It is not aspiration. It is almost everything has been settled; only technical issues are being resolved.
Basically, in Jharkhand, the organ transplant policy is not in a good state, and we are trying to obtain approval for the organ transplant facility.

growth.why: FY27 revenue target INR260 crore (about 50% over FY26's INR173.5 crore) with at least 22% EBITDA margin, backed by cardiac bed expansion, Philips Azurion cath lab, cancer bed expansion to 150 (INR2-3 crore capex) and an acquisition, but no quarterly split and bone marrow transplant revenue pushed to FY28, so backing is partial.
